newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Airways to form airline alliance.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Airways to form airline alliance.

text.p: South African Airways announced on Monday that it had a signed a memorandum of understanding with SA Express Airways and SA Airlink on a proposed alliance between the three airlines.
It said in a statement that the formation of the alliance would position South African Airways (SAA), SA Express Airways (SAX) and SA Airlink as the leading aviation network in Africa.

The objective of the proposed alliance was to provide an integrated national aviation system which would service all routes ranging from entry level to the national hubs and offer national and over-border air transportation.
Further development of the alliance could lead to establishing common shareholding between the airines, SAA said.
The state-owned SAA would continue to service routes between Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban, secondary hubs as well as some peak-time flights between the larger regional centres and the hubs.
SAX and SA Airlink would concentrate on more frequent flights on the routes most suited to their respective 50 and 30 seater aircraft.
"The formation of this powerful alliance is a great step forward for all three airlines," Zukile Nomvete, executive director of transport parastatal Transnet, said.
"We envisage that this partnership will be of great advantage to each member airline, while at the same time adding value to the service provided to the flying public."
The South African government has said it plans to sell more than 30 percent of SAA as part of its overall privatisation programme.
Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said last week that government aimed to speed up the sale of a stake in the airline because of growing competition in the market.
